bdx_002: You can recognise it as the tallest tree in the garden, at 38 metres. It stands on the central lawn of the Jardin Public, a few paces from the ginkgo.
bdx_003: You can recognise it by its bare, sparsely branched winter silhouette, fenced off behind a safety perimeter. It stands on the central lawn of Parc Bordelais.
bdx_004: You can recognise it by its large glossy evergreen leaves with a rust-coloured underside, growing straight out of the paving. It stands on Place Gambetta.
bdx_005: You can recognise it by its wide, spreading crown, 27 metres across, and thick trunk. It stands in the Jardin Public, on Cours de Verdun.
bdx_007: You can recognise it by its short trunk breaking into a dense sheaf of near-vertical branches, like an upturned broom. It stands beside the lake in Parc Bordelais.
